history.period: Swayambhu linga, attributed to Satya Yuga / Treta Yuga tradition (verify)
history.summary: Shri Mankameshwar Mahadev Mandir on the Yamuna bank near Saraswati Ghat (Fort Road, Kydgang) is a wish-fulfillment (mannat) Shiva temple with a black-stone swayambhu shivalinga. Puranic tradition (Shiva, Skanda and Padma Puranas, cited by local sources) identifies this as Kameshwar Tirtha, where Shiva reduced Kamadeva to ashes; the linga is said to have manifested in Satya Yuga, and Rama performed its jalabhishek during his exile after resting at Akshayavat. Folk belief holds that 51 days of sincere prayer here frees one from debts (verify), and the linga is said to grow slightly each Maha Shivaratri (verify). Heavy crowds on Shravan Mondays. DISTINCT-TEMPLE FLAG: this is the Prayagraj (Saraswati Ghat/Yamuna) Mankameshwar, NOT the Mankameshwar Temple of Agra (seq 1081/2356, id mankameshwar-temple-agra / mankameshwar-temple-agra-duplicate) nor the Lucknow one (seq 1057, id mankameshwar-mandir-lucknow). CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Allahabad' - the city was officially renamed Prayagraj in 2018; documented as Prayagraj.

name: Mankameshwar Mandir, Allahabad
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is the sacred city at the Triveni Sangam - the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati - and the site of the Kumbh and Magh Melas. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre as well as a historic city with the Mughal-era Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and Prayagraj University.

travel.road: Fort Road, Kydgang, on the Yamuna bank near Saraswati Ghat, ~2 km from Sangam; auto-rickshaw, taxi or local bus; free parking at premises
